# Wounds, infection and death

## In short
- **A wound left untreated overnight turns into an infection.** The new infection is applied after the night's death checks, so the earliest it can kill you is the following night [1].
- **An infection is a coin flip each night.** It kills you with a 50% chance in default towns and 75% in Pandemonium, checked before the zombie attack [1] [2] [3].
- **Treat wounds the same day.** A Bandage removes the wound. Paracetoid 7g cures an infection and blocks new infections until the attack [4] [5].
- **Being wounded costs you 1 AP a day.** Your maximum AP drops to 5, and some wounds also block specific actions [6].

## How it works

### Getting wounded
- **How a wound is applied.** You can only carry one wound at a time: an already wounded citizen cannot be wounded again. A wound adds `tg_meta_wound` plus one random location from `wound1` to `wound6` (head, hand, arm, leg, eye, foot), and awards the `r_wound_#00` picto [6].
- **Blocked by `tg_stats_locked`.** While this status is set, no status can be inflicted or removed, wounds included [6].

Sources of wounds:
- **Desperate escape** from a zone the zombies control. It always wounds you and gives a 5-minute escape timer. It is not allowed if you are already wounded, terrorised or wearing camouflage [7] [8].
- **Aggression by another citizen.** The target is wounded with chance `OptModifierAttackChance`: 0.5 by default, 0.6 in Pandemonium. An already wounded citizen cannot be attacked [9] [3].
- **Night watch.** If zombies get past the town defences ("overflow"), a watcher who survives may be hit. The game then picks wound or terror, weighted by the two chances [1] [10]. The chances are:
  - Wound chance = 1 − (1 − c)(1 − r), where c is the base death chance plus watch fatigue [11].
  - Base death chance c is 8%. Fatigue for earlier watches adds 0/1/4/9/20/30/42/56/72/90% (Pro-Watchman table: 0/1/4/9/15/20/30/40/50/60/75/90%) [11].
  - r = 0.2 for wounds (0.3 in Pandemonium) and 0.1 for terror (0.2 in Pandemonium) [11].
  - Example on a first watch (c = 0.08): about 26% wound and 17% terror; in Pandemonium about 36% wound and 26% terror (my arithmetic from the formula).
  - A watcher wounded during the attack does not get the wound infection that night [1].
- **A ghoul drinking water** is wounded [12] [13].
- **Sandball hit** (only during the Christmas event). A target who is not already wounded is wounded with chance `OptModifierSandballNastyness`: 0.1 default, 0.0 in small towns, 0.85 in Pandemonium [14] [15] [3].

### Effects of a wound
**Effects of any wound:**
- **Less AP.** Maximum AP is 5 instead of 6, and the daily AP refill sets you to this maximum [6] [1]. The status cards say you "restore 1AP less whenever you drink, eat or rest" [16].
- **Blocked actions.** You cannot make a desperate escape [8], explore a ruin, or attack a citizen [17].
- **Night-watch penalties.** Every wound card lists `nw_death=0.1` and `nw_def=-15` [16].

**Effects by wound location:**

| Wound | Specific effect |
|---|---|
| Head (`wound1`) | Your messages can be distorted with random groans [18] |
| Hand (`wound2`) | No bare-hand zombie attack [8]. No weapon attacks, safe, or opening a First Aid Kit [19] [20] [21]. No repairs [22] |
| Arm (`wound3`) | Cannot build or repair constructions [23] |
| Leg (`wound4`) | Each of your own moves has a 20% chance to fail: you lose 1 AP and stay put. When you lead an escort, each escorted citizen with a leg wound also rolls 20%, and a failure stops the whole group [8] |
| Eye (`wound5`) | Desert dig chance ×0.5. Building search and explorable-ruin dig chance −0.2 [11] |
| Foot (`wound6`) | No specific effect found |

### Infection
**Sources:**
- **Untreated wound, every night.** A wounded, non-infected citizen gets `tg_meta_winfect`, which becomes `infection`. This happens in stage 3, after the day change [1].
- **Infectious poisoned food or items** inflict infection when consumed [24].
- **Contaminated zones.** When `OptFeatureAllPoison` is on, each consumption has a 5% chance to infect you [25].
- **Fireworks destroyed.** Half (rounded up) of the non-infected, non-ghoul citizens in town are infected [26].
- **Shaman healing.** On a successful heal, the status passes back to the healer 5% of the time [27].
- **Event items:**
  - Christmas candy: 30% weighted outcome [28].
  - Halloween `angry_soul` in your chest: 50% [29].
  - April Fools ooze [1].

**Death check:** before the attack (stage 1), an infected citizen who is not a ghoul dies with chance `OptModifierInfectDeath`, minus 0.25 with `good_smell` [1].

### Healing
- **Bandage.** Requires a wound and no `healed` status. It removes the wound and gives `healed`, which is cleared at night and stops a second heal that day. `healed` itself has `nw_death=0.05` and `nw_def=-15` [4] [30].
- **Paracetoid 7g.** It is a drug, so a second dose while drugged makes you addicted. Every version gives `immune`. If you are infected it also removes the infection [5].
- **Shaman.**
  - Cost: 2 MP as the shaman role, or 2 AP as the shaman job [27].
  - Effect: removes one random status among terror, infection, drunk and drugged, with a 65% chance. The target can only be treated once per day, and the cost is paid even on failure [27].

### Immunity
- **`immune` (Immunised)** blocks normal infection unless the infection is forced. It also blocks ghoul infection, which is converted into a normal infection first. It is cleared at night and gives −0.01 night-watch death [6] [31].
- **`immune` does not stop wound infection.** In the code, the immune check runs before `tg_meta_winfect` is converted into `infection` [6]. So immunity alone does not stop a wound from infecting you; bandage the wound.
- **Ghouls** cannot get thirst, infection or wound infection, and lose any infection at the day change [6] [1].

### Death causes
The game defines these causes [32]:
- Dehydration (1), Strangulation (2), Cyanide (3), Hanging (4), Vanished (5), NightlyAttack (6), Addiction (7), Infection (8), Headshot (9), Unknown (10)
- Poison (11), GhulEaten (12), GhulBeaten (13), GhulStarved (14), FleshCage (15), ChocolateCross (16), ExplosiveDoormat (17), Haunted (18), Radiations (19), Apocalypse (20), LiverEaten (21), RabidDog (22)

**Nightly order:**
1. **Outside the town.** Citizens hidden or camping survive with their camping chance; anyone else outside dies as Vanished [1].
2. **Status deaths.** In order:
   - thirst at `thirst2` → dehydration (not ghouls);
   - infection → chance-based death;
   - addiction without the `drugged` status → addiction;
   - a ghoul with hunger > 40 → starvation.

   These bodies are not reanimated for that night's attack [1] [33].
3. **The attack.**
   - Watchers die with their computed death chance [1].
   - A citizen at home dies if more zombies attack the house than its defence (zombies > home defence) [1].
   - Attacking a ghoul always kills it (GhulBeaten) [9].
   - If the reactor is destroyed, every living citizen dies of Radiations [26].

## What changes it
- **`good_smell`** [1] [11]:
  - −25% infection death chance;
  - 25% chance to avoid the wound infection;
  - night-watch wound and terror set to 0;
  - −25 to terror at home.
- **Heroic statuses:**
  - `hsurvive`: immune to all status deaths [1].
  - `hsurvive3`: protects against thirst and infection deaths [1].
  - `hsurvive2` (Cheat Death): protects against the statuses in the hero's immune list. The Cheat Death skill sets this list to thirst, infection, addiction and hunger. When the action was gifted, the giver's list is used [34] [1].
- **`tg_infect_wtns`** (Great Plague victim, per the summary): gives a 50% chance to avoid one infection, then the status is lost [25].
- **Night-watch modifiers:**
  - Death chance: Guardroom −5%, Battlements at level 3 −1%, Automatic sprinklers +4%, ghoul −5% [11].
  - Death chance: each pool bath −1%, but never below the 8% base [11].
  - Terror chance: Gas gun +10% [11].
  - Wound and terror chance: home shower −2.5% each [11].
  - Terror at watch: blocked by `small_catapult3_#00` [1].
- **Preventative Medicine** (hero skill, 361 hero days): you start each town with a First Aid Kit in your chest [35]. The kit can contain Paracetoid (weight 100 out of 1100) or a Bandage (weight 5 out of 1100) [21].

## Town types

| Setting | Default | Small | Pandemonium |
|---|---|---|---|
| Infection death chance | 0.5 | 0.5 | 0.75 |
| Wound chance on citizen aggression | 0.5 | 0.5 | 0.6 |
| Citizen aggression | allowed | blocked (`OptModifierAttackProtect`), unless a ghoul is alive in town | allowed |
| Sandball wound chance | 0.1 | 0.0 | 0.85 |
| Night-watch wound / terror ratio | 0.2 / 0.1 | 0.2 / 0.1 | 0.3 / 0.2 |
| Night-watch death chance | as computed | as computed | doubled (when positive) |

Sources: [2] [15] [3] [9] [11].

- **Remote towns:** I found no differences in the documents I read.
- **Custom towns:** these values are town settings, so they can be changed (for example `OptModifierInfectDeath`).

## Not verified
- I did not confirm in the code that the `nw_death` and `nw_def` card properties feed `getNightWatchDeathChancePenalty` and night-watch defence.
- I did not read how `woundOrTerrorChances` is defined in the code; the "wound + terror" hit chance comes from the summary only.
- I found no specific effect for the foot wound (`wound6`). I did not find what action the Infirmary provides, or what gives `good_smell`.
- I did not read where `OptModifierAttackChance` is set to 0.5 by default; only the Pandemonium diff (0.6 vs default 0.5) shows it.
- The eye-wound ×0.5 case is shown in a code excerpt without the name of its branch; I assumed it is the desert dig.
